descripcion: At B1 you fix the most common verbs that take a gerund (enjoy, avoid) versus an infinitive (want, decide). The verbs that change meaning depending on which form follows come later, once the basic pattern is automatic.

ejemplos.texto: I really enjoy reading before bed.
I want to travel more this year.
I decided to study English seriously.

notas: Enjoy, finish and avoid are always followed by the gerund (-ing), never the infinitive.
Want, decide and hope are always followed by the infinitive (to + verb).
After a preposition, English always uses the gerund: interested in learning.

contraste.es: El español usa el infinitivo de forma más general después de casi cualquier verbo, sin la distinción sistemática entre gerundio e infinitivo que exige el inglés.

errores: Using the infinitive after enjoy, finish or avoid.
Using the gerund after want, decide or hope.
Using the infinitive after a preposition instead of the gerund.
autochequeo: Is the gerund used after enjoy, finish and avoid?
Is the infinitive used after want, decide and hope?
Is the gerund used after every preposition?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on gerunds and infinitives. Check each verb against the pattern it requires and check the gerund after every preposition. Do not rewrite the text.
